# Adjudication Task — Chapter 251

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃251화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|제갈균이 이겼을 거라는 예상은 보기 좋게 빗나갔다.
  6|
  7|그를 비롯한 몇 개의 비무가 치러지고 있는 장소를 찾았을 때, 우리를 기다리던 것은 무적신검을 연호하는 관중들의 함성과 멍하니 앉아 있는 제갈균이었다.
  8|
  9|“뭐야, 졌어?”
 10|
 11|내 물음에 제갈균이 씁쓸하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 12|
 13|“완전히 농락당했습니다. 털끝 하나 못 건드렸어요.”
 14|
 15|제갈균은 오대세가 중 하나인 제갈세가의 직계다.
 16|
 17|신기묘룡이라는 별호로 알 수 있듯 진짜 무기는 명석한 두뇌였지만, 가문의 절학을 익힌 만큼 일신에 지닌 무공도 뛰어났다.
 18|
 19|십봉룡은 단순히 머리만 좋다고 해서 얻을 수 있는 이름이 아니니까.
 20|
 21|‘그런 녀석이 농락당했다고?’
 22|
 23|그렇다면 명백히 한두 수 위의 강자라는 소리다.
 24|
 25|불쑥 호기심이 치밀어 제갈균에게 물었다.
 26|
 27|“어디 있어?”
 28|
 29|“비무 직후 바로 빠져나갔을…… 어? 저기 있군요.”
 30|
 31|제갈균이 가리킨 방향을 바라본 나는 눈매를 좁혔다.
 32|
 33|“저놈이야? 만두 처먹고 있는 놈?”
 34|
 35|“예.”
 36|
 37|“……음.”
 38|
 39|“왜 그러세요?”
 40|
 41|“아냐. 뭔가 익숙한 느낌이라.”
 42|
 43|펑퍼짐한 장포에 깊이 눌러쓴 죽립. 얼굴도 체형도 제대로 보이지 않았지만 쉴 새 없이 만두를 처먹는 옆 모습이 어딘지 모르게 낯익다.
 44|
 45|‘어디서 봤지?’
 46|
 47|이럴 때 정답은 정공법이다. 나는 무적신검을 향해 걸음을 옮겼다.
 48|
 49|한 걸음씩 가까워질수록 기억 속은 흐릿해졌지만, 딱 거기까지였다. 대신 한 가지는 알겠다.
 50|
 51|‘강하다.’
 52|
 53|허술하기 짝이 없는 자세와 태평해 보일 정도로 경계 없는 모습.
 54|
 55|그러나 무적신검에게서 느껴지는 기운은 결코 내 아래가 아니었다.
 56|
 57|이런 놈이 있었나?
 58|
 59|나는 고민 끝에 입을 열었다.
 60|
 61|“저기요.”
 62|
 63|와구와구.
 64|
 65|신들린 듯이 만두를 씹어 삼키던 무적신검의 입이 우뚝 정지했다.
 66|
 67|“무적신검. 맞으시죠?”
 68|
 69|“…….”
 70|
 71|“초면에 실례하겠습니다. 뭐 좀 여쭤볼 게 있어서요.”
 72|
 73|“…….”
 74|
 75|“저기요?”
 76|
 77|뭐야, 이놈. 사람이 부르는데 왜 대답을 안 해.
 78|
 79|빤히 바라보고 있자 죽립 아래로 보이는 무적신검의 목울대가 크게 일렁였다.
 80|
 81|꾸울꺽.
 82|
 83|“큼. 크흠.”
 84|
 85|“……?”
 86|
 87|“커흐흠. 자, 잠시만.”
 88|
 89|몇 번 목을 가다듬은 끝에 무적신검의 입술 사이로 낮은 중저음이 흘러나왔다.
 90|
 91|하지만 뭐랄까, 억지로 꾸며 낸 티가 팍팍 난다.
 92|
 93|“왜요, 가 아니라 무슨 일이오?”
 94|
 95|“뭐 좀 여쭤볼 게 있어서요.”
 96|
 97|“말씀하세요. 아니 하시오.”
 98|
 99|“…….”
100|
101|뭐 하는 놈이야 이거.
102|
103|게슴츠레한 눈으로 무적신검을 바라봤다. 그런 낌새를 눈치챘는지 그가 죽립을 더욱 깊게 눌러썼다.
104|
105|이거 뭔가 느낌이 오는데. 나는 슬쩍 미끼를 던졌다.
106|
107|“아, 제 소개가 늦었네요. 저는 태원박가의 박태경입니다.”
108|
109|“어? 언제 성 바꾸셨어요?”
110|
111|“…….”
112|
113|“……!”
114|
115|싸늘한 침묵. 자신의 실수를 깨달은 무적신검이 허둥지둥 손을 내저었다.
116|
117|꾸며 낸 중저음 대신 소년의 그것처럼 맑고 청명한 목소리가 다급하게 말을 쏟아 냈다.
118|
119|“아니, 그게 아니고요. 산서잠룡이 워낙 유명하니까 알고 있었어요.”
120|
121|“아. 그러시구나.”
122|
123|“네. 네.”
124|
125|“혹시 성함이?”
126|
127|“무적신검이요.”
128|
129|“별호 말고. 성함.”
130|
131|“가, 강풍이요.”
132|
133|무슨 풍?
134|
135|작명 센스 봐라. 어이가 없어진 나는 피식 실소를 흘렸다.
136|
137|이건 굳이 [기감] 스킬로 확인할 필요도 없는 문제였다. 이 정도까지 왔는데 모르는 게 더 이상하지.
138|
139|“오랜만인데 조용한 곳에서 얘기 좀 합시다.”
140|
141|“……왜, 왜요. 전 그쪽 처음 뵙는데요?”
142|
143|“그래? 그럼 화산파에 전서구 날려 줘?”
144|
145|“……!”
146|
147|무적신검이 슬그머니 죽립을 들어 올렸다.
148|
149|천진난만한 인상의 청년이 체념과 반가움이 뒤섞인 눈빛으로 나를 바라보고 있었다.
150|
151|“안녕하세요, 은인.”
152|
153|일 년 만에 보는 반가운 얼굴.
154|
155|나는 청풍의 죽립을 툭 치며 웃었다.
156|
157|
158|
159|* * *
160|
161|
162|
163|무림맹은 하나의 도시에 가까웠다. 사람이 살 수 있는 거주지와 각종 생활을 위한 시설도 모두 갖춰져 있었다.
164|
165|그렇다 보니 유흥가가 있는 것도 그리 놀라운 일은 아니다.
166|
167|우리는 가장 후미진 골목의 객잔에 자리를 잡았다.
168|
169|그곳에는 이미 너무 늙어 귀가 어두운 주인장을 제외하면 어떤 손님도 보이지 않았다.
170|
171|“소식은 들었어요. 화산파 돌아가는 길에 도망쳤다면서?”
172|
173|“네에. 은인이 적 할아버지랑 떠나고 나서 바로요.”
174|
175|“왜 그랬습니까? 고향이나 다름없는데.”
176|
177|“돌아가기 싫었어요. 가 봤자 할아버지도 없고, 세상 구경도 많이 못 해 봤단 말이에요.”
178|
179|“그래도 용케 도망쳤네.”
180|
181|“사질들이 막길래 힘 좀 썼거든요. 아마 사흘 동안은 못 깨어났을 거예요. 그 틈에 얼른 도망쳤어요. 헤헤.”
182|
183|“…….”
184|
185|아니, 도대체 어느 정도로 힘을 쓴 거야.
186|
187|여하간 그것도 청풍 정도는 되어야 가능한 일이다.
188|
189|화산일학이니, 매화삼절이니 해도 청풍은 이미 궤를 달리하는 진짜 천재였으니까.
190|
191|삼류들이나 익히는 삼재 검법이라도 그의 손에서 펼쳐지면 절정 무공이다.
192|
193|지켜본 바에 의하면 그는 무공을 이해하는 깊이나 습득하는 속도가 타의 추종을 불허했다.
194|
195|‘또 다른 천재가 있다고 하면 진무경 정도겠지.’
196|
197|나는 이런저런 생각을 하며 청풍의 신나는 강호 유람기를 들었다.
198|
199|충분히 예상은 했지만, 역시나 무공 수련은 쥐뿔도 안 하고 실컷 돌아다니며 놀고먹은 이야기만 가득했다.
200|
201|“사천에서 만두를 먹었는데 매웠어요!”
202|
203|“아, 예. 그거 되게 놀랍네요.”
204|
205|“광동과 해남의 만두에는 해산물이 들어가요!”
206|
207|“그렇죠. 바다랑 가까우니까.”
208|
209|“절강성 만두는…….”
210|
211|이 자식은 일 년 내내 만두만 처먹었나.
212|
213|나는 결국 호남성 만두에 관한 이야기를 듣다가 참지 못하고 말을 잘랐다.
214|
215|“그래서, 앞으로 어떻게 할 겁니까?”
216|
217|“뭐가요?”
218|
219|“무적신검. 앞으로도 그렇게 있을 거예요?”
220|
221|“네. 백무성 사질이 제가 성라대연에 참가할 거라는 사실을 알고 있거든요. 이렇게 감추면 아무도 못 알아볼 거예요!”
222|
223|“…….”
224|
225|“헤헤. 다들 감쪽같이 속고 있어요.”
226|
227|이미 들켰다는 것에 내 오른손과 전 재산 건다. 거기에 묻고 더블로 갈 용의도 있다.
228|
229|‘어쩐지 아까 비무대 근처에 화산파 제자들이 많더라니.’
230|
231|성라대연은 천하 무림인을 대상으로 하는 만큼 개방적인지라, 마음먹고 신분을 감추더라도 별다른 제약이 없다.
232|
233|다만 구파일방 중 하나인 화산파라면 청풍의 존재를 진즉 눈치챘을 것이 분명했다.
234|
235|그런데도 그저 멀리서 지켜본다는 건…….
236|
237|‘이 정도면 단체 몰카네.’
238|
239|청풍 쇼. 뭐 이런 제목으로 영화 한 편 만들어져도 이상하지 않지.
240|
241|내심 혀를 차며 즐거워하는 청풍을 바라보던 나는 문득 드는 생각에 입을 열었다.
242|
243|“그럼 나중에 만나겠네요?”
244|
245|청풍의 만면에 서린 웃음이 진해졌다.
246|
247|“그랬으면 좋겠네요.”
248|
249|“그랬으면 좋겠다?”
250|
251|“네. 저는 은인이 얼마나 강해졌을지 궁금했거든요. 꼭 한번 겨뤄 보고 싶었어요.”
252|
253|그건 나도 마찬가지다.
254|
255|성라대연에 참가하기로 다짐한 이유 중 하나는 청풍과 진무경의 존재 때문이기도 했으니까.
256|
257|“다시 보니까 어떻습니까?”
258|
259|“음…….”
260|
261|“솔직하게.”
262|
263|나는 낡은 의자에 비스듬히 등을 기댔다.
264|
265|삐걱거리는 소음 속, 잠시 말이 없던 청풍이 돌연 허리에 매어 둔 검집을 툭 쳤다.
266|
267|“할아버지가 그러셨어요. 무인은 병장기로 말해야 한다.”
268|
269|“맞는 말씀 하셨네요.”
270|
271|오랜만에 듣는 검성 피셜이다. 피식 웃은 나는 자리에서 일어났다.
272|
273|“은인, 어디 가세요?”
274|
275|“결승 준비하러. 남은 얘기는 거기서 합시다. 물론 각자의 무공으로.”
276|
277|“결승…….”
278|
279|천천히 그 단어를 읊조린 청풍이 드물게 진지한 표정으로 고개를 끄덕였다.
280|
281|“좋아요. 어차피 제가 우승할 거지만.”
282|
283|“꿈도 크셔. 일 년 내내 만두만 먹어 놓고.”
284|
285|“무공 수련도 가끔 했다고요.”
286|
287|“퍽이나.”
288|
289|청풍의 볼멘소리를 흘려들으며 값을 치르고 객잔을 나왔다.
290|
291|그리고 좁고 어두운 골목을 빠져나오자마자 익숙한 얼굴과 맞닥트렸다.
292|
293|“종리추?”
294|
295|종리추가 웃으며 손을 흔들었다.
296|
297|“오, 여기서 또 보는군. 역시 우리는 인연이 있는 모양일세.”
298|
299|“인연은 무슨. 우연이겠지. 그런데 여긴 어쩐 일이야?”
300|
301|“요기나 하러 왔지.”
302|
303|“굳이 여기서?”
304|
305|후미진 골목길에는 나란히 늘어선 가게 몇 개가 전부였다. 그것도 낡아서 허물어지기 직전인.
306|
307|누가 봐도 끼니를 해결하기에는 딱히 좋은 선택지처럼 보이지 않는다.
308|
309|하지만 종리추는 태연하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
310|
311|“근처 노점에서 소면을 먹었는데, 글쎄 노점상 주인이 말하길 저 가게 만두가 그렇게 맛있다지 뭔가.”
312|
313|그가 가리키는 간판은 공교롭게도 나와 청풍이 막 나온 바로 그 가게였다.
314|
315|“그래?”
316|
317|“물론일세. 아는 사람만 아는 맛집이라던데. 혹시 먹어 봤나?”
318|
319|어느새 죽립을 푹 눌러쓴 청풍이 어색한 변조 목소리로 불쑥 끼어들었다.
320|
321|“엄청나게 맛있어요. 아니, 맛있소.”
322|
323|종리추의 시선이 청풍을 향했다.
324|
325|“처음 보는 친구로군. 혹시 누구인지 물어보면 실례가 될까?”
326|
327|“무적신검 강풍.”
328|
329|“별호 한번 멋지군. 나는 상승검 종리추일세. 앞으로 잘 부탁하네, 친구.”
330|
331|“치, 친구?”
332|
333|살짝 죽립을 들어 종리추를 바라본 청풍이 세차게 고개를 끄덕였다.
334|
335|“좋아요! 아니, 좋네! 기쁘네! 내게 먼저 친구가 되자고 한 사람은 자네가 처음일세!”
336|
337|“……그만. 그 정도면 충분해.”
338|
339|차라리 이마에 화산파의 청풍이라고 붙이고 다니지 그러냐.
340|
341|기뻐서 날뛰는 청풍과 그런 녀석을 진정시키는 내 모습을 본 종리추가 부드럽게 미소지었다.
342|
343|“이미 곁에 좋은 친구를 둔 것 같은데 뭘. 여하간 다음에 보세, 친구들.”
344|
345|“어, 웬만하면 어쩌다 한번 보자고. 너무 자주는 말고.”
346|
347|“잘 가게! 잘 가게, 친구여!”
348|
349|“참고하지.”
350|
351|그는 고개를 까딱 숙이고 어두컴컴한 골목으로 사라졌다.
352|

*If there’s another genius like him, it would have to be Jin Mukyung.*

“Here?”

“Really?”

[P159]

[P162]

[P164]

[P167]

[P172]

[P173]
“Farewell! Farewell, my friend!”

[P174]
“I’ll keep that in mind.”

“Oh, I should’ve told him to use only a little soy sauce.”

[P181]
“…”

[P182]
He really didn’t listen to a word I said.

[P183]
* * *

[P184]
Cheongpung’s concern proved unnecessary.

[P185]
Jongni Chu never entered the inn.

[P186]
His steps didn’t stop even after he passed it.

[P187]
He walked through the maze of dark alleys until, at last, he stopped in a place inhabited only by rats and filth.

[P188]
A quiet voice slipped from his lips.

[P189]
“The Invincible Divine Sword. The more I think about it, the better that epithet sounds. What do you think?”

[P190]
The moment he finished speaking, the silent alley erupted into motion.

[P191]
*Swish, swish, swish! Pak!*

[P192]
Three streaks of light shot toward Jongni Chu’s vital points.

[P193]

[P194]

[P195]
*Thud.*

[P196]
“Where are you going in such a hurry?”

[P197]
“…!”

[P198]
“Come down. Let’s talk.”

[P199]

[P200]

[P201]
*How can this be?!*

[P202]
He had completed hundreds of missions, but never once had anything like this happened.

[P203]
Overwhelming. Irresistible.

[P204]

[P205]
*Pavilion Master, it seems this is as far as I go.*

[P206]
The face of the superior he had loyally served for decades—the Thousand-Faced Fox—flashed before his eyes.

[P207]
Shadow Killer, the finest agent of the now-forgotten Hidden Shadow Pavilion, prepared to bite down on the poison pellet hidden in his tooth.

[P208]
“As expected of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion. Not a moment’s hesitation. But…”

[P209]
*Thud-thud-thud.*

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 251

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃251화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|제갈균이 이겼을 거라는 예상은 보기 좋게 빗나갔다.
  6|
  7|그를 비롯한 몇 개의 비무가 치러지고 있는 장소를 찾았을 때, 우리를 기다리던 것은 무적신검을 연호하는 관중들의 함성과 멍하니 앉아 있는 제갈균이었다.
  8|
  9|“뭐야, 졌어?”
 10|
 11|내 물음에 제갈균이 씁쓸하게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 12|
 13|“완전히 농락당했습니다. 털끝 하나 못 건드렸어요.”
 14|
 15|제갈균은 오대세가 중 하나인 제갈세가의 직계다.
 16|
 17|신기묘룡이라는 별호로 알 수 있듯 진짜 무기는 명석한 두뇌였지만, 가문의 절학을 익힌 만큼 일신에 지닌 무공도 뛰어났다.
 18|
 19|십봉룡은 단순히 머리만 좋다고 해서 얻을 수 있는 이름이 아니니까.
 20|
 21|‘그런 녀석이 농락당했다고?’
 22|
 23|그렇다면 명백히 한두 수 위의 강자라는 소리다.
 24|
 25|불쑥 호기심이 치밀어 제갈균에게 물었다.
 26|
 27|“어디 있어?”
 28|
 29|“비무 직후 바로 빠져나갔을…… 어? 저기 있군요.”
 30|
 31|제갈균이 가리킨 방향을 바라본 나는 눈매를 좁혔다.
 32|
 33|“저놈이야? 만두 처먹고 있는 놈?”
 34|
 35|“예.”
 36|
 37|“……음.”
 38|
 39|“왜 그러세요?”
 40|
 41|“아냐. 뭔가 익숙한 느낌이라.”
 42|
 43|펑퍼짐한 장포에 깊이 눌러쓴 죽립. 얼굴도 체형도 제대로 보이지 않았지만 쉴 새 없이 만두를 처먹는 옆 모습이 어딘지 모르게 낯익다.
 44|
 45|‘어디서 봤지?’
 46|
 47|이럴 때 정답은 정공법이다. 나는 무적신검을 향해 걸음을 옮겼다.
 48|
 49|한 걸음씩 가까워질수록 기억 속은 흐릿해졌지만, 딱 거기까지였다. 대신 한 가지는 알겠다.
 50|
 51|‘강하다.’
 52|
 53|허술하기 짝이 없는 자세와 태평해 보일 정도로 경계 없는 모습.
 54|

[P118]
They could make a whole movie out of it and call it *The Cheongpung Show*.

[P119]
I clicked my tongue inwardly as I watched Cheongpung enjoying himself. Then a thought occurred to me.

[P120]
“Then I guess we’ll meet later.”

[P121]
The smile on Cheongpung’s face widened.

[P122]
“I hope so.”

[P123]
“You hope so?”

[P124]
“Yes. I was curious how strong Benefactor had become. I’ve wanted to spar with you at least once.”

[P125]
The feeling was mutual.

[P126]
Cheongpung and Jin Mukyung were two of the reasons I had decided to participate in the Star-Array Grand Banquet.

[P127]
“What do you think, now that you’ve seen me again?”

[P128]
“Hmm…”

[P129]
“Be honest.”

[P130]
I leaned back in the old chair.

[P131]
Cheongpung was silent for a moment amid the chair’s creaking. Then he tapped the scabbard at his waist.

[P132]
“Grandpa used to say that martial artists should speak with their weapons.”

[P133]
“He was right.”

[P134]
Straight from the Sword Saint himself.

[P135]
I let out a quiet laugh and rose from my seat.

[P136]
“Where are you going, Benefactor?”

[P137]
“To prepare for the finals. We’ll finish this conversation there—with our martial arts.”

[P138]
“The finals…”

[P139]
Cheongpung slowly repeated the word, then nodded with an unusually serious expression.

[P140]
“Good. I’m going to win anyway.”

[P141]
“Big talk from someone who spent the entire year eating dumplings.”

[P142]
“I trained sometimes too.”

[P143]
“Sure you did.”

[P144]
Ignoring Cheongpung’s disgruntled muttering, I paid the bill and left the inn.

[P145]
As soon as we emerged from the narrow, dark alley, we ran into a familiar face.

[P146]
“Jongni Chu?”

[P147]
Jongni Chu smiled and waved.

[P148]
“Oh, we meet again. It seems we must be bound by fate.”

[P149]
“What fate? It’s probably just a coincidence. What are you doing here?”

[P150]
“I came to grab a bite.”

[P151]
“Here?”

[P152]
The secluded alley held only a few shops lined up beside one another. Even those looked so old they were on the verge of collapsing.

[P153]
It didn’t look like a good place to find a meal by anyone’s standards.

[P154]
But Jongni Chu nodded calmly.

[P155]
“I had some thin noodles at a nearby street stall, and the vendor told me that shop’s dumplings were exceptionally good.”

[P156]
By sheer coincidence, he was pointing at the sign of the very inn Cheongpung and I had just left.

[P157]
“Really?”

[P158]
“Of course. Apparently, it’s a hidden gem known only to a select few. Have you tried it?”

[P159]
Cheongpung, who had already pulled his bamboo hat low over his face, abruptly joined in with his awkwardly altered voice.

[P160]
“They’re incredibly delicious. No—I mean, they are delicious.”

[P161]
Jongni Chu turned toward Cheongpung.

[P162]
“I don’t believe we’ve met. Would it be rude of me to ask who you are?”

[P163]
“The Invincible Divine Sword, Kang Pung.”

[P164]
“Now that is an impressive epithet. I’m Jongni Chu, the Always-Victorious Sword. I hope we’ll get along, friend.”

[P165]
“F-Friend?”

[P166]
Cheongpung raised his bamboo hat slightly and stared at Jongni Chu before nodding furiously.

[P167]
“Great! No—I mean, good! I’m delighted! You’re the first person who’s ever asked to be my friend!”

[P168]
“…Enough. That’s more than enough.”

[P169]
Why didn’t he just walk around with *Cheongpung of Huashan* written across his forehead?

[P170]
Jongni Chu smiled gently as he watched Cheongpung bouncing with joy while I tried to calm him down.

[P171]
“It seems you already have a good friend at your side. In any case, I’ll see you next time, friends.”

[P172]
“Yeah, let’s just happen to run into each other once in a while. Not too often.”

[P173]
“Farewell! Farewell, my friend!”

[P174]
“I’ll keep that in mind.”

[P175]
He dipped his head and disappeared into the dark alley.

[P176]
Once we stepped onto the bright, sunlit street, Cheongpung grinned.

[P177]
“He seems like a good person. I can just tell.”

[P178]
I offered him some serious advice.

[P179]
“Not everyone who likes dumplings is a good person.”

[P180]
“Oh, I should’ve told him to use only a little soy sauce.”

[P181]
“…”

[P182]
He really didn’t listen to a word I said.

[P183]
* * *

[P184]
Cheongpung’s concern proved unnecessary.

[P185]
Jongni Chu never entered the inn.

[P186]
His steps didn’t stop even after he passed it.

[P187]
He walked through the maze of dark alleys until, at last, he stopped in a place inhabited only by rats and filth.

[P188]
A quiet voice slipped from his lips.

[P189]
“The Invincible Divine Sword. The more I think about it, the better that epithet sounds. What do you think?”

[P190]
The moment he finished speaking, the silent alley erupted into motion.

[P191]
*Swish, swish, swish! Pak!*

[P192]
Three streaks of light shot toward Jongni Chu’s vital points.

[P193]
At the same time, a small masked figure soared into the air. His steps were swift and silent as the wind as he raced along the wall.

[P194]
His movement technique was exceptional, and his concealment technique surpassed even that. Just as the masked man gathered his strength to leap—

[P195]
*Thud.*

[P196]
“Where are you going in such a hurry?”

[P197]
“…!”

[P198]
“Come down. Let’s talk.”

[P199]
An immense force pressed down on both his shoulders. Breath brushed the back of his neck.

[P200]
The masked man’s plummeting body trembled as if struck by lightning.

[P201]
*How can this be?!*

[P202]
He had completed hundreds of missions, but never once had anything like this happened.

[P203]
Overwhelming. Irresistible.

[P204]
Never had those words felt so real. He realized that only one path remained to him.

[P205]
*Pavilion Master, it seems this is as far as I go.*

[P206]
The face of the superior he had loyally served for decades—the Thousand-Faced Fox—flashed before his eyes.

[P207]
Shadow Killer, the finest agent of the now-forgotten Hidden Shadow Pavilion, prepared to bite down on the poison pellet hidden in his tooth.

[P208]
“As expected of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion. Not a moment’s hesitation. But…”

[P209]
*Thud-thud-thud.*

[P210]
Lightning-fast fingers struck points all across Shadow Killer’s body. As he went rigid, a low voice burrowed into his ear.

[P211]
“You should have known who you were following.”

[P212]
Consumed by utter despair, Shadow Killer felt his consciousness plunge into the abyss.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
